t:8c658f6d6f48: Jobs, 25, tells Apple's story from the garage to the Apple II. He calls the computer a "bicycle for the mind", talks about VisiCalc and ease of use, and sketches where personal computing is heading.
t:e8484f0e1cf7: Raw ABC 20/20 footage shot at Apple's offices on 18 Feb 1981, with reporter Bob Brown. Jobs, 25, explains why personal computers matter; unedited, so you see the crew between takes.
t:e16465a77172: Jobs, 28, gives his "The Future Isn't What It Used to Be" talk to designers: the history of computers, industrial design and how media evolves. Apple exists, he says, because it found the "fractional horsepower computer" five years before anyone else.
t:2a91330003ee: Apple's full 24 Jan 1984 meeting at the Flint Center. Jobs shows the "1984" ad, pulls the Mac out of a bag and it says "Hello, I'm Macintosh". It ends with a Q&A with the Mac team.
t:1fe9ec0d0469: Jobs unveils the Macintosh: the "1984" ad, demos of MacWrite and MacPaint, the Mac introducing itself, and a standing ovation.
t:922abd5e4e8c: At the Apple II Forever event in April 1984, Jobs reviews the Mac's first 100 days, with about 70,000 sold, and shows the software already written for it.
t:375a3763e3e7: Jobs and the first NeXT employees at company retreats: Paul Rand shows the team his proposed NeXT logo, and they brainstorm product and software priorities. Around 11:00 Joanna Hoffman stands up to Jobs over his "reality distortion field" on the due date.
t:05c277a8b273: Jobs's public launch of the NeXT Computer, three years after leaving Apple. The full footage was thought lost until researchers for Aaron Sorkin's Steve Jobs film found it on a pair of VHS tapes.
t:3f43c8e5be60: A long TV interview: the computer as a bicycle for the mind, VisiCalc, desktop publishing, "interpersonal computing", Engelbart and Xerox PARC, the Homebrew Computer Club, the Blue Box and Wozniak.
t:c5ab7a52ee06: A confidential, employees-only video in which Jobs explains NeXT's competitors and go-to-market plan at a whiteboard. He sizes the professional workstation market at about 100,000 units in 1991, with Sun holding about 80%.
t:8ef3d2ba304b: A July 1991 interview, probably by Brent Schlender for Fortune's "Ten Years of the PC" piece. Jobs is clearly annoyed that "the PC" means the IBM PC, when the Apple II came four years earlier.
t:eb71dde38409: Filmed in Redwood City on 19 Dec 1991 for a documentary about quality pioneer Joseph Juran. Jobs says the main lesson NeXT took from Juran: treat everything as a repeatable process, then measure how it's running.
t:ff5fad1cbb02: Jobs shows off Release 3 of NeXTSTEP, including sending an email to a colleague about Ross Perot, who had invested $20 million in NeXT.
t:96555e4cd1f1: A spring 1992 talk to MIT Sloan MBA students: being forced out of Apple, the challenges of portable technology and his management style. He also says "PowerBooks are pretty good, but the Quadra sucks wind."
t:a1b0806e2769: A long oral-history interview at 40: childhood and Heathkits, firing underperformers, Microsoft's monopoly and Sculley, Xerox PARC in 1979, the Web, Pixar and Toy Story, and death as life's greatest invention.
t:09c9cbb5e5e0: The full, unedited 1995 one-on-one oral-history interview, recorded for the Computerworld Information Technology Awards Foundation.
t:6bfc32f8cf5e: Robert Cringely's interview for the PBS series Triumph of the Nerds. Only 9 of its 69 minutes aired and the master tapes were lost, until the director found a copy in his garage after Jobs died.
t:6ef3643dfc46: The short cut of Robert Cringely's interview, as it aired in the 1995 PBS documentary Triumph of the Nerds on the birth of the PC.
t:bb6fdff86499: Jobs's SIGGRAPH 1995 keynote, months before Toy Story opened. He walks through 100 years of film, from the Lumière brothers to Star Wars, then Toy Story's numbers: 800,000 machine-hours of rendering and over 600 textures for Buzz.
